title: El Nino-linked floods hit Peru and Ecuador; Ecuador reports 34 deaths
location: Piura, Peru; Manta and other areas, Ecuador
summary: Heavy rains linked to El Nino flooded cities in northern Peru and Ecuador. Ecuador's risk management agency reported 34 deaths and 47,000 people affected nationwide, while about 2,000 families were affected in Piura, Peru, where a hospital ward had to be moved. Peru's navy said heavy swells damaged coastal infrastructure and forced the temporary closure of dozens of ports, and forecasters warned of several more days of rain.
impact_assessment: Observed: deaths, displacement and damage to health facilities and port infrastructure in Peru and Ecuador. Potential: further flooding as an El Nino episode projected to be among the strongest on record develops, with knock-on effects on shipping, fisheries and food security.
priority_rationale: MODERATE: a deadly and spreading climate-driven disaster with infrastructure impact; single wire-based source so far.

reported_claims.text: 34 people have died and 47,000 have been affected by El Nino-linked heavy rains nationwide.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Ecuador National Secretariat for Risk Management

reported_claims.text: Some 2,000 families have been affected by the rains in Piura, according to preliminary reports.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Luis Vasquez, head of Peru's National Institute of Civil Defense

reported_claims.text: Heavy ocean swells damaged infrastructure on the Pacific coast and forced the temporary closure of dozens of ports.
Moderate to heavy rain could continue in parts of the region for four days.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Peru National Meteorology and Hydrology Service

reassessment_triggers: Rising death toll or mass displacement
